{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (1873–1953)}}
[[File:Johan Antony Barrau.jpg|thumb|Johan Antony Barrau]]
'''Johan Antony Barrau''' (3 April 1873, [[Oisterwijk]] – 8 January 1953, Utrecht) was a Dutch mathematician, specializing in geometry.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=Johan Antony Barrau|website=University of Groningen, History|url=http://www.cs.rug.nl/jbi/History/Barrau}}</ref>

Barrau was educated at the [[Royal Naval College (Netherlands)|Dutch Royal Naval College]] at [[Willemsoord, Den Helder|Willemsoord]] and then at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. From 1891 to 1898, Barrau was an officer with the [[Royal Netherlands Navy]], later with the [[Netherlands Marine Corps]]. However, he left the service and became a mathematics teacher at a [[Hogere Burgerschool]] in [[Dordrecht]] until 1900, then in Amsterdam.<ref name=Bio/> In 1907 he obtained his PhD at the [[University of Amsterdam]] under the supervision of [[Diederik Korteweg]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=30596}}</ref> From 1908 to 1913 Barrau was a mathematics professor at the [[Delft University of Technology]]. He was a professor of synthetic, analytical and descriptive differential geometry at the [[University of Groningen]] from 1913 to 1928.<ref name=Bio/> From 1928 until his retirement at age 70, he was a professor at [[Utrecht University]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Soifer, Alexander|title=The Scholar and the State: In Search of Van der Waerden|page=171|publisher=Springer Basel|year=2015|isbn=9783034807128|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=F_VWBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA171}}</ref> He received the military service medal consisting of the [[Expedition Cross|Expedition Cross with the Atjeh clasp]] and was named Knight of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]]. Barrau published a textbook on analytical geometry and various articles in national and international journals.<ref name=Bio/>

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1920 at Strasbourg<ref>{{cite book|author=Barrau, J. A.|chapter=Sur la cinématique plane|pages=590–593|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=msu.31293001749500;view=1up;seq=640|year=1921|title=Compte rendu du Congrès international des mathématiciens tenu à Strasbourg du 22 au 30 Septembre 1920|series=ICM proceedings|publisher=University of Toronto Press}}</ref> and in 1924 at Toronto.<ref>{{cite journal|title=The International Congress at Toronto|author=Dresden, Arnold|authorlink=Arnold Dresden|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=31|year=1925|issue=1–2|pages=1–10|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1925-03982-8|doi-access=free}} (See p. 6.)</ref>
